claims.evidence: Witness only reports a generic car engine bay/partial assembly; no make/model, engine code, or cylinder count is readable from the shown angles.
No documentation, import papers, or markings confirming Belgium origin are shown.
Photos show an engine bay on a shop floor, but no running video, dashboard/OBD readout, or test sheet is shown.
No audio/video of startup or running is provided in the witness report.
No odometer/ECU mileage readout or service record is shown.
Photos do not show tamper evidence clearly (e.g., seal marks, opened covers, or proof of assembly integrity).

risks.risk: Exact engine compatibility (Hyundai vs Kia, engine code, year, ECU/wiring/harness match) is unknown; wrong fit can make it unusable or costly to adapt.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine identification plate/engine code stamping (and ECU part number) plus the full engine label area; also a photo of the transmission mating side/engine mounts to confirm configuration.
risks.if_unproven: Price as an unverified used engine assembly with unknown compatibility (worst-case: may require parts/rewiring/ECU swap).

risks.risk: Whether it truly runs and has no internal damage (knock, misfire, compression loss) cannot be confirmed from static photos.
risks.proof: Short video of cold start and idle (with hood open), plus an OBD scan screenshot showing no active fault codes.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven running/health (worst-case: may need overhaul).

risks.risk: Engine completeness: starter, alternator, ECU, wiring harness, sensors, and any turbo/ancillaries may be missing or partially wrapped/covered.
risks.proof: A full inventory photo/clip laid out (starter, alternator, ECU, harness, all sensors/hoses) and a wide shot showing the entire engine from front to back with no plastic wrap covering key components.
risks.if_unproven: Price as partial/possibly incomplete assembly (worst-case: buyer must source missing components).

risks.risk: Hidden mechanical condition (timing chain/belt, water pump, oil pump, bearings, seals) cannot be assessed from the engine bay alone.
risks.proof: Compression test and/or leak-down test results (photos of gauge readings) and photos of timing cover area (or service records showing recent timing service).
risks.if_unproven: Price as unknown wear items (worst-case: timing service and reseal may be required).

risks.risk: Potential damage or corrosion not visible in the shown angles (cracks, bent components, coolant/oil contamination) could affect reliability.
risks.proof: High-resolution photos of critical areas: cylinder head surface, block casting for cracks, oil pan underside, coolant passages, and any visible fluid staining; plus close-ups of mounting points.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used with unknown condition (worst-case: may have leaks or internal issues).

proof_requests: Clear photos of the engine identification plate/engine code stamping and ECU part number (so we can confirm exact Hyundai/Kia 4-cylinder variant).
Video of the engine starting from cold and running at idle (hood open), plus a short clip showing steady RPM.
OBD scan screenshot showing no active fault codes (or fault codes if present).
Photos showing the full engine with all plastic wrap removed, and a checklist/inventory of included parts (starter, alternator, ECU, wiring harness, sensors).
Compression test and/or leak-down test results (photos of gauge readings) and photos of oil/coolant condition.
response.reason: The witness confirms it is a used car engine bay/partial assembly, but the key details needed to price safely in Lagos (exact engine code/compatibility and verified running/health) are not shown. Without proof of running and compatibility, any price would be guesswork.
